## Sabır: kendini tutmak, birbirini tutmak

Türkçede sabır çoğu zaman edilgen bir bekleyiş, başa geleni sessizce çekmektir. Arapça kelimenin işi tutmaktır: {ar:الصبر حبس النفس عن الجزع, tr:es-sabru habsu'n-nefsi ani'l-ceza', gloss:sabır nefsi feryattan alıkoymaktır, source:"ص ب ر,B001"}; {ar:صبرت نفسي أي حبستها, tr:sabartu nefsî ey habestuhâ, gloss:nefsimi tuttum, alıkoydum, source:"ص ب ر,B001"}. Karşıtı da açıkça adlandırılır: {ar:الصبر نقيض الجزع, tr:es-sabru nakîdu'l-ceza', gloss:sabır feryadın karşıtıdır, source:"ص ب ر,B001"}. Kur'an insanın kendi hâlini tam bu karşıtla anlatır ve bu surenin kalıbıyla bir istisna kurar: {ar:إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا, tr:inne'l-insâne hulika helû'â, gloss:insan pek tez canlı yaratıldı, source:70:19}, {ar:إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعًۭا, tr:izâ messehu'ş-şerru cezû'â, gloss:kötülük dokununca feryat eder, source:70:20}, {ar:وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا, tr:ve izâ messehu'l-hayru menû'â, gloss:iyilik dokununca esirger, source:70:21}, {ar:إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ, tr:ille'l-musallîn, gloss:namaz kılanlar hariç, source:70:22}. Orada da "insan" tekil bir hükümle anılır, ardından bir topluluk ayrılır. Feryat eden insan, sabrın yokluğunda kalan insandır.

Tutmanın ters yüzü de aynı kelimededir: kendini tutmayan, tutulur. Araplar öldürülmek üzere bağlanıp alıkonmuş hayvana {ar:المصبورة المحبوسة على الموت, tr:el-masbûratu'l-mahbûsetu ale'l-mevt, gloss:ölüme alıkonmuş olan, source:"ص ب ر,B002"} derlerdi. Sabır ya kişinin kendine yaptığı bir tutmadır ya da başkasının ona yaptığı. Birinci ayetin kelimesi de alıkoymak diye açıklanır {source:"ع ص ر,B006"}; tutmanın bu iki yönünün buluştuğu sahne surenin bütününe aittir, bu ayetin payı kişinin kendi nefsini tutmasıdır. Oruç da bu tutmanın bir türü sayılırdı: {ar:سمي الصوم صبرا لكونه كالنوع له, tr:summiye's-savmu sabran, gloss:oruç, sabrın bir türü olduğu için sabır diye anıldı, source:"ص ب ر,B015"}. Beklemek de öyle: {ar:فاصبر لحكم ربك أي انتظر حكمه, tr:fasbir li-hukmi rabbik, ey intazır hukmeh, gloss:Rabbinin hükmüne sabret, yani hükmünü bekle, source:"ص ب ر,B014"}. Bekleyiş burada bir kendini tutma biçimidir; gevşeyip dağılmadan, zamanı gelene kadar yerinde durmak.

Bu tutmanın somut aletleri de kökte vardır. Şişenin ağzını kapatan tıpaya {ar:الصبار صمام القارورة, tr:es-sıbâru simâmu'l-kârûra, gloss:sıbâr, şişenin tıpasıdır, source:"ص ب ر,B018"} denirdi; kabın kenarlarına da {ar:أصبار الإناء نواحيه, tr:esbâru'l-inâ', gloss:kabın kenarları, source:"ص ب ر,B004"}. Tıpa içtekinin dökülmesini ve uçup gitmesini önler; kabın kenarı sıvıyı bir arada tutar. İkisi de içerideki şeyi korumak için sınır çizer. Sabır, bu imgenin yanında, insanın içindekini dökülmekten koruyan kenardır. Kur'an sabrı bir kaptan boşaltılan şey gibi anlatır. Firavun'un sihirbazları Musa'nın Rabbine inandıklarında Firavun onlara ellerini ve ayaklarını çaprazlama kestirip asacağını söyler {source:7:124}; onlar şöyle cevap verir: {ar:وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ إِلَّآ أَنْ ءَامَنَّا بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَآءَتْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَآ أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًۭا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ, tr:ve mâ tenkımu minnâ illâ en âmennâ bi-âyâti rabbinâ lemmâ câetnâ, rabbenâ efrig aleynâ sabran ve teveffenâ muslimîn, gloss:bizden yalnızca Rabbimizin ayetleri bize gelince onlara inandığımız için öç alıyorsun; Rabbimiz, üzerimize sabır boşalt ve bizi Müslüman olarak öldür, source:7:126}. İman ile sabır burada da yan yanadır: iman edildiği için gelen tehdide, kaptan dökülür gibi gelen bir sabır istenir. Calût'un ordusunun karşısına çıkanlar da aynı duayı eder ve ayaklarının sağlam basmasını ister {source:2:250}.

Sabrın kendisi bir ilacın da adıdır: {ar:الصبر بكسر الباء عصارة شجرة, tr:es-sabir, gloss:sabir, bir ağaçtan sıkılan özdür, source:"ص ب ر,B008"}, {ar:الصبر هذا الدواء المر, tr:es-sabru hâze'd-devâu'l-murr, gloss:sabır, bu acı ilaç, source:"ص ب ر,B008"}. İlaç ağzı acıtır ama iyileştirir; işi hoşa gitmekle değil, bünyeyi düzeltmekle ölçülür. Birinci ayetin kelimesi sıkmayı da adlandırdığı için {source:"ع ص ر,B002"}, sıkılan ve sonunda bir öze dönüşen şeyin sahnesi surenin bütününde kurulur; bu ayetin payı o özün adı olan son kelimedir. Sabrın sertliği de taşta duyulur: {ar:الصبرة من الحجارة ما اشتد وغلظ, tr:es-subra mine'l-hicâra, gloss:taşlardan sert ve kalın olanı, source:"ص ب ر,B005"}; dağa da bu kökten ad verilir: {ar:الصبير الجبل, tr:es-sabîru'l-cebel, gloss:sabîr, dağdır, source:"ص ب ر,B017"}. Sabrın gerektiği yer de bir adla anılır: {ar:أم صبور أمر لا منفذ له عنه, tr:ummu sabûr, gloss:çıkış yolu olmayan iş, source:"ص ب ر,B006"}; kışın kemiğe işleyen soğuğu da öyle: {ar:صبارة الشتاء شدة برده, tr:sabâratu'ş-şitâ', gloss:kışın sert soğuğu, source:"ص ب ر,B007"}. Sabır, çıkışın olmadığı yerde ve soğuğun en sert anında kişinin yerinde durmasıdır.

Bu ayetin sabrı ise tek kişinin değil, birbirine iletilen bir sabırdır. Kök bunu da adlandırır: {ar:الصبير هو الكفيل, tr:es-sabîru huve'l-kefîl, gloss:sabîr kefildir, source:"ص ب ر,B003"}. Kefil, bir başkasının borcunun arkasında duran kişidir; borçlu ödeyemezse ödeme ona düşer. Araplar bir topluluğun kefiline şöyle derlerdi: {ar:صبير القوم الذي يصبر لهم ويكون معهم في أمورهم, tr:sabîru'l-kavmi'llezî yasbiru lehum ve yekûnu meahum fî umûrihim, gloss:topluluğun sabîri, onlar için katlanan ve işlerinde onlarla birlikte duran kişidir, source:"ص ب ر,B003"}. Birbirine sabrı tavsiye eden topluluk, bu imgenin yanında, birbirinin kefili olan bir topluluktur: biri gevşediğinde öteki onun yerine tutar. Bulutların bile birbirini taşıdığı söylenirdi: {ar:السحاب الأبيض الذي يصبر بعضه فوق بعض درجا, tr:es-sehâbu'l-ebyadu'llezî yasbiru ba'duhû fevka ba'd, gloss:basamak basamak birbirinin üstünde duran beyaz bulut, source:"ص ب ر,B010"}.

Kur'an sabrı bir topluluğun yanında durmak olarak da emreder. Allah Peygamber'e der ki: {ar:وَٱصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلْعَشِىِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُۥ ۖ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا, tr:vasbir nefseke ma'allezîne yed'ûne rabbehum bi'l-gadâti ve'l-aşiyyi yurîdûne vecheh, ve lâ ta'du aynâke anhum turîdu zînete'l-hayâti'd-dunyâ, gloss:sabah akşam Rablerine O'nun rızasını isteyerek dua edenlerle birlikte nefsini tut; dünya hayatının süsünü isteyerek gözlerin onlardan ayrılmasın, source:18:28}. Sabır burada bir yerde durmaktır, ama yalnız değil, bir topluluğun yanında. İman edenlere de karşılıklı bir sabır söylenir: {ar:يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱصْبِرُوا۟ وَصَابِرُوا۟ وَرَابِطُوا۟, tr:yâ eyyuhe'llezîne âmenû'sbirû ve sâbirû ve râbitû, gloss:ey iman edenler, sabredin, sabırda birbirinizle yarışın ve bağlı durun, source:3:200}.

Sabrın bir de ters yüzü vardır ve o da tutmaktır, ama yanlış şeye: {ar:الصبر الجرأة ومنه فما أصبرهم على النار, tr:es-sabru'l-cur'a, gloss:sabır cüret anlamına da gelir; "ateşe ne kadar da dayanıklılar" sözü buradandır, source:"ص ب ر,B013"}. Kur'an bu sözü, Allah'ın indirdiği kitaptan bir kısmını gizleyip az bir bedele satanlar için söyler: {ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْعَذَابَ بِٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ ۚ فَمَآ أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ, tr:ulâike'llezîne'şteravu'd-dalâlete bi'l-hudâ ve'l-azâbe bi'l-magfira, fe-mâ asbarahum ale'n-nâr, gloss:onlar hidayete karşılık sapıklığı, bağışlanmaya karşılık azabı satın alanlardır; ateşe ne kadar da dayanıklılar, source:2:175}. Kendini tutmak, yanlış bir alışverişe direnmeye de dönüşebilir. Ayetin sıralaması bu yüzden anlamlıdır: sabır, haktan sonra gelir ve onun ardından tavsiye edilir.

Sabrın karşılığı da kendi kelimesinin bir kullanımında duyulur. Araplar tartmadan, ölçmeden yığın hâlinde alınan mal için {ar:اشتريت الشيء صبرة أي بلا وزن ولا كيل, tr:iştereytu'ş-şey'e subraten, gloss:malı yığın hâlinde, tartmadan ve ölçmeden aldım, source:"ص ب ر,B011"} derlerdi. Kur'an'da Peygamber'e, iman eden kullara Rablerinden sakınmalarını, Allah'ın yerinin geniş olduğunu söylemesi emredilir ve söz şöyle biter: {ar:إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ, tr:innemâ yuveffe's-sâbirûne ecrahum bi-gayri hisâb, gloss:sabredenlere ücretleri ancak hesapsız olarak tam ödenir, source:39:10}. Kelimenin bir kullanımı tartısız alınan yığını, ayet tartısız ödenen ücreti anlatır.

## Hakka dayanan sabır

Hak ile sabır Kur'an'da birbirine dayanarak gelir. Peygamber'e iki ayrı yerde aynı cümle söylenir: {ar:فَٱصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ, tr:fasbir inne va'dallâhi hakk, gloss:sabret; Allah'ın vaadi haktır, source:40:55}. İkincisi bir uyarıyla devam eder: {ar:فَٱصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ ۖ وَلَا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُوقِنُونَ, tr:fasbir inne va'dallâhi hakkun ve lâ yestehıffenneke'llezîne lâ yûkınûn, gloss:sabret, Allah'ın vaadi haktır; kesin bilgiye ermemiş olanlar seni hafifliğe sürüklemesin, source:30:60}. Sabrın dayanağı hakkın kendisidir: vaat yerine oturacağı için beklemek anlamlıdır. Hakkı olmayan sabır cürete, sabrı olmayan hak ise hafifliğe döner; kesin bilgiye ermemişlerin sürüklediği şey de budur. Bu ayet ikisini ayrı ayrı tavsiye eder ama aynı sırayla: önce yerine oturan şey, sonra onu tutmanın gücü.

Bir babanın oğluna öğüdü bu sırayı bir hayat içinde gösterir. Lokman oğluna öğüt verirken önce ona Allah'a ortak koşmamasını söyler {source:31:13}; sözün arasına Allah'ın kendi sözü girer: {ar:وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ, tr:ve vassayne'l-insâne bi-vâlideyh, gloss:insana anne babasını tavsiye ettik, source:31:14}. Tavsiye fiili ve ikinci ayetin "insan"ı aynı cümlededir. Lokman öğüdünü şöyle bitirir: {ar:يَٰبُنَىَّ أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَٱنْهَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَكَ ۖ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ, tr:yâ buneyye ekımi's-salâte ve'mur bi'l-ma'rûfi venhe ani'l-munkeri vasbir alâ mâ esâbek, inne zâlike min azmi'l-umûr, gloss:yavrum, namazı dosdoğru kıl, iyiliği emret, kötülükten alıkoy ve başına gelene sabret; bunlar kararlılık gerektiren işlerdendir, source:31:17}. Doğruyu söyleyen kişinin başına bir şey gelir; öğüt bunu bilir ve sabrı söylenen doğrunun hemen ardına koyar. Bu ayetteki sıra da aynıdır: hakkı birbirine ileten topluluk, o hakkın bedelini taşımak için birbirine sabrı da iletir.

Bu sabrın en ileri işi, kopmuş olanı birbirine eklemektir. Allah iyilik ile kötülüğün bir olmadığını söyler ve kötülüğü en güzel olanla savmayı emreder: {ar:فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةٌۭ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِىٌّ حَمِيمٌۭ, tr:fe-izellezî beyneke ve beynehû adâvetun keennehû veliyyun hamîm, gloss:bir de bakarsın, seninle arasında düşmanlık olan kişi sanki candan bir dost olmuştur, source:41:34}; ardından bu işin kime nasip olduğu söylenir: {ar:وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا۟, tr:ve mâ yulakkâhâ illellezîne saberû, gloss:buna ancak sabredenler kavuşturulur, source:41:35}. Bu da bir istisnadır ve yine sabredenleri ayırır. Aralarında düşmanlık olan iki kişinin dost olması, birbirinden ayrı düşmüş iki öbeğin birleşip tek bir yeşillik olmasına benzer; o birleşmeyi taşıyan güç de nefsi feryattan alıkoyan, birbirinin kefili olan sabırdır.

## Whole surah (Arabic)

103:1	وَٱلْعَصْرِ
103:2	إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
103:3	إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ

const r = await tools.exec_command({
  cmd: `cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/103_3/luna/list.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.8.16	truth spoken reciprocally	The commentary makes truth something members pass to one another; Zechariah commands neighbors to speak truth to each other and judge for peace, turning haqq into communal practice.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lev.19.17	rebuke a neighbor	The ayah's repeated reciprocal counsel is concrete here: Israel must reprove a neighbor openly rather than harbor hatred, making correction a duty owed to another.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.17	iron sharpens iron	The commentary stresses that each person gives and receives counsel; Proverbs explicitly pictures one person sharpening another, a close image of reciprocal moral strengthening.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.25	truth with one's neighbor	The ayah's haqq is passed among a community; Paul tells each member to put away falsehood and speak truth with a neighbor, making truth an interpersonal obligation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.24	stir one another to good works	The commentary says the righteous are defined by mutual exhortation, not only private belief; Hebrews tells believers to provoke one another to love and good works.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.25	encourage one another	The commentary's repeated tawāṣaw makes support reciprocal; Hebrews names mutual encouragement as the community approaches the coming day.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.11	build one another up	The commentary's two final verbs describe giving and receiving counsel; Paul likewise commands the community to encourage and build up one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.14	patience with all	The commentary makes sabr a shared practice; Paul asks the church to admonish the disorderly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.18	deed and truth	The commentary joins righteous action with counsel in haqq; John says love must be shown in deed and truth, joining ethical action to truthfulness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.1.3	work of faith and steadfastness	The commentary's first three traits are belief, work, and patient mutual counsel; Paul praises a community's work of faith, labor of love, and steadfastness of hope in one compact formula.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.2.17	faith without works	The commentary makes belief and righteous deeds distinct but jointly identify the saved; James says faith without works is dead, insisting that belief must take visible form.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.2.22	faith completed by works	The commentary pairs belief with deeds; James reads Abraham's faith as active together with his works and brought to completion by them.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Jas.2.24	works and faith alone	The commentary's exception includes both belief and righteous action; James explicitly says a person is justified by works and not by faith alone, a distinct reading of their relation.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Rom.4.5	faith apart from working	The commentary describes the saved group by belief together with righteous deeds; Paul contrasts the one who does not work but trusts God, a different account of how faith is reckoned righteous.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Eph.2.8	grace through faith	The commentary's list includes righteous deeds among the marks of those rescued from loss; Ephesians says salvation is by grace through faith and not from works, locating its source differently.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.2.10	created for good works	The commentary includes righteous deeds in the saved group's defining pattern; Ephesians says people are created in Christ for good works prepared for them to walk in.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.10	work and love	The commentary treats good action as work whose value is not lost; Hebrews says God remembers the readers' work and love shown in serving the saints.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.12	faith and patience	The commentary places patience after truth and makes it communal; Hebrews urges imitation of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.6	repayment according to works	The commentary links work, a due share, and the day when each meets what is owed; Paul says God repays each according to works.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.7	patiently doing good	The commentary's saved group persists in righteous work and patience; Paul describes those who seek glory through patient endurance in doing good.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.12	endurance, commandments, and faith	The commentary makes patience the companion of truth and faithful action; Revelation identifies the saints by endurance, keeping God's commandments, and faith in Jesus.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.12	reward according to work	The commentary links human work to the day of reckoning; the risen Jesus says his reward is with him to repay each according to their work.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.25.40	acts for the least	The commentary defines the saved through righteous actions; in Matthew's judgment scene, feeding and welcoming the vulnerable count as service to the Son of Man.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58	labor not in vain	The commentary sets righteous work against loss; Paul tells the community its labor in the Lord is not empty, directly answering the fear that work disappears.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.5.10	deeds at judgment	The commentary joins work to the day each person receives what is due; Paul says all must appear before Christ's judgment seat and receive according to what they did.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	endurance before the promise	The commentary makes sabr the strength to bear the cost of truth; Hebrews says believers need endurance so that after doing God's will they may receive the promise.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.2	bear one another's burdens	The commentary's sabr can mean standing as another's guarantor; Paul tells believers to carry one another's burdens, thereby fulfilling Christ's law.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.9	keep doing good	The commentary's patience holds firm through hardship; Paul tells the community not to grow weary in doing good, since the harvest comes in its season.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.8.15	hold fast and bear fruit	The commentary joins inward restraint to good action; Jesus describes hearers who hold the word fast and bear fruit with endurance.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.7	farmer waits for fruit	The commentary uses connected plants and patience through the season; James tells believers to wait like a farmer for the earth's precious fruit.

strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.4	withheld wages	The commentary connects haqq with a debt and a worker's due share; James says unpaid wages cry out against landowners, exposing the injustice of withholding what is owed.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.25	members care for one another	The commentary's guarantor image has one person holding another up; Paul says the body is arranged so its members have the same care for one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.26	shared suffering and honor	The commentary says when one member weakens another bears the load; Paul says if one member suffers all suffer, and if one is honored all rejoice.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.16	body joined and growing	The commentary's connected plants leave no gaps and feed each other; Paul pictures a body joined together as each part works and builds the whole in love.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.24.15	wages due before sunset	The commentary brings work, payment, and the end of the day together; Deuteronomy requires paying a poor laborer before sunset because the wage is his livelihood.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.11.1	fair weights	The commentary names short measure and haqq as a due share; Proverbs condemns false balances and approves an honest weight.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.12.14	every deed judged	The commentary says the Hāqqa brings each person face to face with their work and due; Ecclesiastes says God brings every deed, hidden or open, into judgment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mic.6.8	do justice, love kindness	The commentary makes righteous action more than a label; Micah names the life God requires as doing justice, loving kindness, and walking humbly.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.31.40	work through heat and frost	The commentary makes patience staying put in the hardest cold; Jacob recounts laboring for Laban through daytime heat and nighttime frost while sleep fled from him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.7	trust in the Lord	The commentary hears belief as entrusting oneself to safety; Jeremiah blesses the person whose trust is the Lord.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.8	tree bearing fruit in drought	The commentary joins linked greenery to patient endurance; Jeremiah's trusting person is a tree by water that stays green in heat and keeps bearing fruit in drought.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.55.10	rain gives seed and bread	The commentary's joined plants follow a rain-bearing cloud; Isaiah says rain and snow water the earth, making it sprout and provide seed and food.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.55.11	word accomplishes its work	The commentary treats advice as a word passed on for people to act upon; Isaiah says God's word goes out and accomplishes the purpose for which it was sent.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.25	the Lord is good to those who wait	The commentary interprets patience as remaining in place until the appointed time; Lamentations calls the Lord good to those who wait for him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.26	wait quietly for salvation	The commentary contrasts sabr with panicked outcry; Lamentations says it is good to wait quietly for the Lord's salvation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.31	waiting renews strength	The commentary describes sabr as staying firm through weariness; Isaiah says those who wait for the Lord renew their strength and do not grow faint.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.26.3	steadfast mind and peace	The commentary hears belief as security and sabr as staying steady; Isaiah promises peace to the one whose mind remains steadfast because it trusts God.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.26.4	the everlasting rock	The commentary's hard stone and mountain images make patience a form of firmness; Isaiah calls Israel to trust the Lord as an everlasting rock.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.6.7	teach through the day	The commentary defines mutual counsel as a word passed among people; Deuteronomy commands parents to teach the words diligently and speak of them at home, on the road, lying down, and rising.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.31.12	assemble all to hear and learn	The commentary shifts from the singular human to a believing community; Moses commands the whole assembly, including children and resident aliens, to gather, hear, learn, and observe the teaching.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.31.13	children learn and fear	The commentary treats counsel as something that continues across a community; the next verse says children who have not known the law must hear it and learn reverence.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.3	tree, fruit, and prospering action	The commentary's good deeds are lasting and uncorrupted; Psalm 1 pictures the righteous as a tree bearing fruit in season whose action prospers.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.4	chaff blown away	The commentary sets those rescued from loss against the general human condition; Psalm 1 contrasts the fruitful righteous with wicked people like chaff that wind drives away.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.15.6	Abraham trusts a promise	The commentary hears belief as reliance that gives security; Abraham trusts God's promise of descendants, and that trust is reckoned to him as righteousness.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.7.9	believe and stand firm	The commentary hears iman as becoming secure; Isaiah's warning plays belief against being established, making trust a condition of standing firm.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.3	wait for the appointed vision	The commentary describes sabr as waiting without loosening one's hold; Habakkuk says the vision has an appointed time and commands the reader to wait though it seems slow.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.4	the righteous live by faithfulness	The commentary puts haqq before sabr as the ground for endurance; Habakkuk joins the righteous person's life to faithfulness while the vision is awaited.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.8.17	truth, peace, and false oaths	The commentary says the repeated advice names truth so that harmful speech is not passed along; Zechariah forbids devising evil and false oaths after commanding truthful speech.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lev.19.18	love your neighbor	The commentary makes counsel and the other's due part of a shared life; Leviticus closes its instructions on honest dealing by commanding love of one's neighbor.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.5	open rebuke	The commentary says one believer should remind another of what is owed; Proverbs says open rebuke is better than concealed love.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.6	faithful wounds of a friend	The commentary's counsel can be corrective as well as comforting; Proverbs calls a friend's wounds faithful, unlike an enemy's abundant kisses.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.2.22	toil with no gain	The commentary links work to a due wage and the danger of loss; Qohelet asks what a person gains from all the toil expended under the sun, making the outcome of labor a live question.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.160	word and truth	The commentary makes haqq something reliable that must be passed on; the psalm says the sum of God's word is truth and its righteous judgments endure.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.15.6	faith credited as righteousness	The commentary's first qualification is belief; Genesis gives a concrete instance in Abraham, whose trust in God's promise is counted as righteousness.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.17.12	others hold up a weary leader	The commentary describes sabr as one person standing behind another when they weaken; Aaron and Hur support Moses' hands until sunset so Israel can continue the fight.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Rosh Hashanah 29a	Moses' hands and Israel's gaze	The commentary uses sabr as communal support; the Talmud rereads Moses' raised hands, saying Israel prevailed by looking upward and submitting their hearts to God, not by the hands themselves.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.31.40	labor's cost and endurance	The commentary links work, time, and patience through hardship; Jacob's account of heat, frost, and sleepless service gives a lived scene of endurance within labor.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.4.8	righteous statutes	The commentary's haqq means what is right and binding; Moses asks what nation has statutes and judgments as righteous as Israel's, giving a concrete scriptural form of binding right.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.23.2	lacking nothing under a shepherd	The commentary opens against the human condition of loss; the psalm's speaker says that under the Lord's care he lacks nothing, a contrasting picture of provision.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.16.2	restraint imposed by God	The commentary distinguishes self-restraint in sabr from being held back by another; Sarai says the Lord has restrained her from bearing children, showing the same holding image with a different agent and object.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.27.16	heaped silver and clothing	The commentary recalls a heap of goods taken without weighing; Job says the wicked may pile up silver and clothing, echoing the material heap image without making it patience.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 1:1	transmission from teacher to student	The commentary presents counsel as a word that joins one generation to the next; Avot opens with Moses receiving and handing on Torah through a chain of teachers.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 1:2	world sustained by deeds	The commentary treats righteous actions as what keeps people from loss; Avot says the world stands on Torah, worship, and acts of lovingkindness.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 1:6	friend and teacher	The commentary's reciprocal verb makes each person both giver and receiver of counsel; Avot advises acquiring both a teacher and a companion.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 1:17	action over study	The commentary insists that the saved are identified by work as well as belief; Avot says action, not study alone, is the essential thing.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 2:16	work that one must not abandon	The commentary describes patience as holding steady until work bears fruit; Avot says one need not finish the work but is not free to desist from it.
medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Peah 1:1	deeds with this-world and future fruit	The commentary notes that this ayah names no wage after the opening faith-and-work formula; Peah says acts of lovingkindness yield fruit in this world while their principal remains for the world to come.
medium	tevrat	motif	Ta'anit 23a	planting for a later generation	The commentary's plant image makes each cluster feed the next; Honi's old man plants a carob tree whose fruit he will not live to eat because others planted for him.
medium	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:4	trust and patience in trial	The commentary defines sabr as holding firm when hardship has no exit; Sirach tells the one serving God to accept trial, trust him, and wait for his mercy.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 3:6	faith tested like gold	The commentary calls patience a bitter medicine that improves the person; Wisdom says the righteous were tested like gold in a furnace and found acceptable.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.5.10	prophets as patient examples	The commentary says people who speak truth may bear its cost; James points to the prophets who spoke in the Lord's name as examples of suffering and patience.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.5.11	Job's endurance	The commentary's sabr holds firm in pain and waits for the outcome; James calls Job's endurance blessed and points to the Lord's compassionate end.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.8	faith expressed by action	The commentary pairs belief with work; Hebrews says Abraham obeyed and went out by faith, showing trust enacted rather than only asserted.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.17	faith under test	The commentary joins belief to deeds that define the believer; Hebrews says Abraham offered Isaac by faith when tested.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.20.8	wages at day's end	The commentary connects work to the day's wage; the vineyard owner pays the workers at evening, giving a narrative setting for labor, time, and compensation.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.20.15	generous wage and the worker's claim	The commentary understands haqq as a due share; the owner insists he wronged no worker while paying from generosity, complicating a simple equation of work and proportionate reward.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.26	hearing without doing	The commentary says deeds distinguish those who leave loss; Jesus contrasts the hearer who does not act with the house that collapses in a storm.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.6	one plants, another waters	The commentary's linked vegetation lets one growth meet another; Paul describes different workers planting and watering while God gives the growth.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.2.2	pass the teaching onward	The commentary hears mutual advice as speech that is joined and transmitted; Paul tells Timothy to entrust what he heard to faithful people able to teach others.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Did.4.1	word remembered day and night	The commentary emphasizes repeated advice and the joining of day to night; the Didache tells a learner to remember the one who speaks God's word day and night.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Did.4.2	seek the words of the saints	The commentary pictures each person as both recipient and giver of counsel; the Didache urges believers to seek the faces of the saints daily and rest on their words.
medium	incil	motif	1 Clement 38.1-2	strong care for weak	The commentary's sabr includes a guarantor who stands with others in their affairs; Clement says the strong should care for the weak and the weak should respect the strong.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.15.5	branches bear fruit by remaining	The commentary's plant clusters stay connected and productive; Jesus says a branch bears fruit only by remaining in the vine, making continued attachment the condition of fruitfulness.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.5.16	good works seen by others	The commentary says righteous actions define the saved community; Jesus says visible good works can lead others to glorify the Father.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.20.13	agreed wage	The commentary describes haqq as a debt or rightful share; the owner answers a worker by pointing to the agreed wage, making the claim of what is owed explicit.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.9	fellow workers	The commentary's reciprocal counsel makes a community work together; Paul calls its members God's coworkers, not isolated laborers.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Gen.15.6	אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary's âmanû means belief heard as trust; Hebrew he'emin describes Abraham trusting God's promise, a semantic match for the table's unverified sound correspondence.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.7.9	אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary links belief with becoming secure; Isaiah plays he'aminu against te'amenu, believe against being established, but the table marks the root match as unverified.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.17.12	אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary makes sabr support another until strength returns; the verse calls Moses' hands steady with emunah while Aaron and Hur hold them, a lexical and scene-level echo.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Hab.2.4	אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary joins belief, haqq, and patient waiting; Habakkuk's righteous person lives by emunah, here faithfulness, while awaiting the vision.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.119.160	אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary treats haqq as reliable truth passed between people; the psalm calls God's word emet, truth, from the Hebrew root listed as a sound correspondence to Arabic amn.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Dan.6.4	Aramaic אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary hears iman as trustworthiness as well as belief; Daniel's opponents find no fault because he is faithful, an Aramaic use of the table's corresponding root.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Deut.4.8	חקק; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary's haqq is right that is also binding; Deuteronomy's righteous statutes use the Hebrew root ḥqq, a possible sound correspondence whose legal sense is not identical to haqq.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.23.2	חסר; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary frames humanity as being in loss; the psalm says the shepherded speaker will not lack, using the Hebrew root the table aligns with kh-s-r, though the Arabic root link is unverified.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Job.27.16	צבר; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary explicitly recalls ṣabra as an unmeasured heap of goods; Job uses Hebrew ṣbr for piling silver, a specific heap image, not a claim that Hebrew ṣbr means patience.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.1.3	צלח; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary calls ṣāliḥ action sound and fruitful; the righteous tree's deed prospers with Hebrew ṣlḥ, a possible root correspondence whose sense is success, not the Arabic adjective.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Gen.16.2	עצר; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary pairs sabr's self-restraint with ʿaṣr as holding back; Genesis uses Hebrew ʿṣr when Sarai says God restrained her from bearing, a possible sound link with a different agent.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.2.22	עמל; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary's ʿamal is purposeful work; Qohelet's ʿamal is burdensome toil, a possible cognate that highlights a difference in the word's biblical use.
weak	tevrat	soydas	Targum Onkelos on Genesis 15:6	Aramaic אמנ; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary hears iman as trust; Onkelos renders Abraham's belief as trust in the Lord's Memra and reckons it as merit, an Aramaic root connection that remains unverified.
weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.2.22	עמל; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary associates work with a due wage and an escape from loss; Qohelet asks what gain comes from toil, a specific contrary outcome for the possible עמל correspondence.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.8.16	truth spoken reciprocally	The commentary makes truth something members pass to one another; Zechariah commands neighbors to speak truth to each other and judge for peace, turning haqq into communal practice.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lev.19.17	rebuke a neighbor	The ayah's repeated reciprocal counsel is concrete here: Israel must reprove a neighbor openly rather than harbor hatred, making correction a duty owed to another.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.17	iron sharpens iron	The commentary stresses that each person gives and receives counsel; Proverbs explicitly pictures one person sharpening another, a close image of reciprocal moral strengthening.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.25	truth with one's neighbor	The ayah's haqq is passed among a community; Paul tells each member to put away falsehood and speak truth with a neighbor, making truth an interpersonal obligation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.24	stir one another to good works	The commentary says the righteous are defined by mutual exhortation, not only private belief; Hebrews tells believers to provoke one another to love and good works.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.25	encourage one another	The commentary's repeated tawāṣaw makes support reciprocal; Hebrews names mutual encouragement as the community approaches the coming day.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.11	build one another up	The commentary's two final verbs describe giving and receiving counsel; Paul likewise commands the community to encourage and build up one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.14	patience with all	The commentary makes sabr a shared practice; Paul asks the church to admonish the disorderly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.18	deed and truth	The commentary joins righteous action with counsel in haqq; John says love must be shown in deed and truth, joining ethical action to truthfulness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.1.3	work of faith and steadfastness	The commentary's first three traits are belief, work, and patient mutual counsel; Paul praises a community's work of faith, labor of love, and steadfastness of hope in one compact formula.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.2.17	faith without works	The commentary makes belief and righteous deeds distinct but jointly identify the saved; James says faith without works is dead, insisting that belief must take visible form.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.2.22	faith completed by works	The commentary pairs belief with deeds; James reads Abraham's faith as active together with his works and brought to completion by them.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Jas.2.24	works and faith alone	The commentary's exception includes both belief and righteous action; James explicitly says a person is justified by works and not by faith alone, a distinct reading of their relation.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Rom.4.5	faith apart from working	The commentary describes the saved group by belief together with righteous deeds; Paul contrasts the one who does not work but trusts God, a different account of how faith is reckoned righteous.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Eph.2.8	grace through faith	The commentary's list includes righteous deeds among the marks of those rescued from loss; Ephesians says salvation is by grace through faith and not from works, locating its source differently.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.2.10	created for good works	The commentary includes righteous deeds in the saved group's defining pattern; Ephesians says people are created in Christ for good works prepared for them to walk in.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.10	work and love	The commentary treats good action as work whose value is not lost; Hebrews says God remembers the readers' work and love shown in serving the saints.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.12	faith and patience	The commentary places patience after truth and makes it communal; Hebrews urges imitation of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.6	repayment according to works	The commentary links work, a due share, and the day when each meets what is owed; Paul says God repays each according to works.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.7	patiently doing good	The commentary's saved group persists in righteous work and patience; Paul describes those who seek glory through patient endurance in doing good.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.12	endurance, commandments, and faith	The commentary makes patience the companion of truth and faithful action; Revelation identifies the saints by endurance, keeping God's commandments, and faith in Jesus.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.12	reward according to work	The commentary links human work to the day of reckoning; the risen Jesus says his reward is with him to repay each according to their work.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.25.40	acts for the least	The commentary defines the saved through righteous actions; in Matthew's judgment scene, feeding and welcoming the vulnerable count as service to the Son of Man.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58	labor not in vain	The commentary sets righteous work against loss; Paul tells the community its labor in the Lord is not empty, directly answering the fear that work disappears.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.5.10	deeds at judgment	The commentary joins work to the day each person receives what is due; Paul says all must appear before Christ's judgment seat and receive according to what they did.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	endurance before the promise	The commentary makes sabr the strength to bear the cost of truth; Hebrews says believers need endurance so that after doing God's will they may receive the promise.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.2	bear one another's burdens	The commentary's sabr can mean standing as another's guarantor; Paul tells believers to carry one another's burdens, thereby fulfilling Christ's law.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.9	keep doing good	The commentary's patience holds firm through hardship; Paul tells the community not to grow weary in doing good, since the harvest comes in its season.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.8.15	hold fast and bear fruit	The commentary joins inward restraint to good action; Jesus describes hearers who hold the word fast and bear fruit with endurance.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.7	farmer waits for fruit	The commentary uses connected plants and patience through the season; James tells believers to wait like a farmer for the earth's precious fruit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.8	strengthen your hearts	The commentary's sabr is remaining firm until the appointed time; James says to be patient and strengthen the heart because the Lord's coming is near.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.4.19	do good while entrusting oneself	The commentary joins faith, good work, and patience under threat; Peter tells sufferers to entrust themselves to the faithful Creator while continuing to do good.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.11	painful discipline yields fruit	The commentary calls patience a bitter medicine that can repair what it hurts; Hebrews says discipline is painful at first but later yields peaceful fruit to those trained by it.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.24	hearing and doing	The commentary's good action is a life that holds together rather than collapses; Jesus compares hearing and doing his words to building a house on rock.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.12.20	feed an enemy	The commentary describes patient goodness turning hostility into intimacy; Paul applies Proverbs by telling believers to feed a hungry enemy.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.12.21	overcome evil with good	The commentary presents patient good as the means by which enmity can become friendship; Paul concludes that evil is overcome by good.

strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.8	planting, watering, and wages	The commentary joins work, connected growth, and due payment; Paul says planter and waterer are one and each receives wages according to labor.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.9	God's field and coworkers	The commentary's linked greenery pictures members who nourish one another; Paul calls the church God's field and its workers God's coworkers.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.4.34	no needy person	The commentary makes one person's due share a concern of the whole community; Acts says believers shared possessions so that no one among them was in need.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.6.12	debts between people	The commentary hears haqq as a debt owed by one person to another; the Lord's Prayer makes forgiveness of our debts reciprocal with forgiving our debtors.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.13.8	what is owed to a neighbor	The commentary says mutual counsel recalls what each owes the other; Paul says to pay what is owed and leave no debt outstanding except love for one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.4	withheld wages	The commentary connects haqq with a debt and a worker's due share; James says unpaid wages cry out against landowners, exposing the injustice of withholding what is owed.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.25	members care for one another	The commentary's guarantor image has one person holding another up; Paul says the body is arranged so its members have the same care for one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.26	shared suffering and honor	The commentary says when one member weakens another bears the load; Paul says if one member suffers all suffer, and if one is honored all rejoice.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.16	body joined and growing	The commentary's connected plants leave no gaps and feed each other; Paul pictures a body joined together as each part works and builds the whole in love.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.11.1	fair weights	The commentary names short measure and haqq as a due share; Proverbs condemns false balances and approves an honest weight.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.12.14	every deed judged	The commentary says the Hāqqa brings each person face to face with their work and due; Ecclesiastes says God brings every deed, hidden or open, into judgment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mic.6.8	do justice, love kindness	The commentary makes righteous action more than a label; Micah names the life God requires as doing justice, loving kindness, and walking humbly.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.31.40	work through heat and frost	The commentary makes patience staying put in the hardest cold; Jacob recounts laboring for Laban through daytime heat and nighttime frost while sleep fled from him.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.7	trust in the Lord	The commentary hears belief as entrusting oneself to safety; Jeremiah blesses the person whose trust is the Lord.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.8	tree bearing fruit in drought	The commentary joins linked greenery to patient endurance; Jeremiah's trusting person is a tree by water that stays green in heat and keeps bearing fruit in drought.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.5.27	weighed and found lacking	The commentary connects loss, a rightful share, and final reckoning; Daniel says Belshazzar was weighed in balances and found deficient, combining judgment with the market image.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.21	doing the Father's will	The commentary identifies the saved by belief together with deeds; Jesus distinguishes saying “Lord” from doing the Father's will.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.22	doers of the word	The commentary pairs belief with righteous action; James warns hearers to become doers of the word rather than deceive themselves by hearing alone.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.2	patience bearing with one another	The commentary makes sabr a shared practice; Paul names patience and bearing with one another in love as the conduct that preserves unity.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.18.15	correction that regains a brother	The commentary makes mutual advice a way of holding a community together; Jesus instructs a person to confront a sinning brother privately, and says listening can regain the brother.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.1	restore gently	The commentary joins correction with patience and self-restraint; Paul says to restore a person caught in transgression gently while watching oneself against temptation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.4.2	correction with patience and teaching	The commentary puts truth before sabr because speaking truth may carry a cost; Timothy is told to reprove, rebuke, and exhort with complete patience and teaching.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6	love rejoices with truth	The commentary makes haqq the content of mutual counsel; Paul says love does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices with truth.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7	bearing and enduring	The commentary describes sabr as holding fast for another; Paul says love bears, hopes, and endures all things.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.2.2	works, labor, and endurance	The commentary's traits include work and patience; Revelation praises a church for its works, labor, and patient endurance while testing false claims.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.5	faith joined to virtue	The commentary pairs belief with righteous action; Peter urges believers to supplement faith with virtue and knowledge.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.6	self-control and endurance	The commentary describes sabr as holding oneself steady; Peter's sequence joins self-control to steadfastness and steadfastness to godliness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.7	brotherly affection and love	The commentary's virtues culminate in reciprocal counsel; Peter ends his sequence with brotherly affection and love.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.3	trial produces steadfastness	The commentary calls patience a bitter medicine that forms the person; James says the testing of faith produces steadfastness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.4	endurance brought to completion	The commentary treats sabr as remaining firm until its work is done; James says steadfastness should have its full effect, making the person complete.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.33.4	estranged brothers embrace	The commentary says patient good can turn enmity into intimacy; Esau runs to embrace Jacob after their long estrangement and fear.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Chr.20.20	trust, prophetic counsel, and success	The commentary hears belief as security and counsel as something passed on; Jehoshaphat tells Judah to trust God and the prophets, with the promise that they will stand and prosper.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.3.7	a time to speak and be silent	The commentary joins truthful counsel to self-restraint; Qohelet's paired times for silence and speech give a concrete limit and occasion for words.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.9.10	work while life remains	The commentary ties work to limited time and the day of reckoning; Qohelet urges wholehearted work now, saying there is no work or knowledge in Sheol.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.15.1	a soft answer turns away anger	The commentary imagines truthful counsel replacing dispute; Proverbs says a gentle answer turns away wrath, showing how speech can interrupt conflict.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.21	feed a hungry enemy	The commentary says good conduct can turn an enemy into a friend; Proverbs instructs the reader to feed an enemy who is hungry.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.22	coals on an enemy's head	The commentary reads kindness toward an enemy as reconciliation; Proverbs adds that feeding the enemy heaps coals on his head, a consequence often read as shame or repentance but whose force is debated.
